A1.justification: Both PDFs contain readable versions of the same GIDD research, including equations, experimental displays and appendices. Relocated material can be matched, including v1 Appendix I becoming v2 H.9 and v1 Appendix J becoming v2 Appendix I.

before.justification: V1 reports original OpenWebText experiments, downstream benchmark evaluations, self-correction results and model-scaling analyses in Section 5 and Appendices A–D.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds GPT-4o assessments of generated text and empirical entropy measurements.

M1.justification: The stated hybrid noising kernel changes from an all-ones uniform component to u=(1-m)/(N-1), explicitly excluding the mask token (Section 4). This is a limited specification revision; implementation changes or retraining are not established. The architecture, sampling algorithm and self-correction procedure remain, while the main ELBO rewrite is algebraically equivalent.

E1.justification: Both use OpenWebText, the same seven downstream benchmarks, unconditional generation and self-correction scenarios. GPT-4o grading and entropy add measurements of retained generation tasks, rather than new datasets or task coverage.

E2.justification: V2 Table 5 removes the TinyLlama 1.1B and MDM 1.1B reference comparisons reported in v1 Table 4. GPT2, retrained Llama, reimplemented MDM, MD4 and MDLM remain in their corresponding comparisons. GPT-4o serves as an evaluator, not a competing generation method.

E3.justification: V2 substantially expands sample-quality evaluation with unigram entropy and GPT-4o grading on five 1–10 quality dimensions (Sections 5.3–5.4, Appendix F.1). The grading comparison specifies self-correction temperatures for each noise setting. Existing training budgets, validation splits and downstream likelihood-evaluation procedures are retained.

E4.justification: V2 adds systematic checks of whether perplexity improvements correspond to qualitative improvements or diversity loss. These include GPT-4o before/after grading and entropy analyses across self-correction, denoising-step and min-p settings (Table 4; Figures 3, 5, 6 and 8). Existing weighting ablations, scaling analyses and generation examples remain.

E5.justification: V2 Table 4 introduces statistical difference markers defined as greater than 2σ or 5σ, absent from v1. The PDFs do not establish additional training runs, and the new grading analysis does not specify its sample count or how these statistical differences were calculated.

E6.justification: V2 adds a substantial set of grading scores and entropy findings. For example, Table 4 reports clarity increasing from 2.49 to 2.90 after self-correction for pu=0.2 at temperature 0.5, while mask-only clarity falls from 2.51 to 1.99. These are newly reported evaluations, not gains between paper versions. Tables 2–3 and the retained downstream benchmark rows preserve their scores.

T1.justification: Beyond the equivalent KL-plus-Itakura–Saito ELBO reformulation, v2 adds an alternative full-divergence bound under nonnegative weights in Remark H.6 and substantially replaces the global-minimum proof with an argument addressing zero-weight intervals. Appendix H.8 also introduces an extra B factor in Equation 65 that conflicts with the derivative summarized in Equation 69.

C1.justification: The central claims remain the generalized interpolating framework, closed-form transitions and ELBO, compute-matched leading diffusion perplexity, and self-correction enabled by hybrid noise. V2 foregrounds an already-present global-minimum guarantee and adds evidence supporting the retained quality claims.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly distinguishes likelihood-based benchmark performance from generation quality and argues that multiple-choice benchmarks alone are insufficient. It qualifies v1's overfitting explanation with run-to-run variation and possible short-document bias from random cropping. Appendix G additionally explains that entropy detects severe diversity collapse but can miss subtler losses.

D1.justification: Appendix F.1 newly specifies the gpt-4o-2024-08-06 evaluator, grading categories and output procedure, with the prompt displayed in Figure 7; Appendix F explains entropy computation. Training hardware and hyperparameters remain. The abstract retains the code link but drops the explicit statement that models are open-source, without establishing any actual withdrawal.

R1.justification: V2 adds focused references on sequence-generation errors, nonmonotonic generation, adaptive diffusion ordering and weighting, and sampling evaluation. Section 6 explicitly acknowledges Austin et al.'s earlier masking-plus-uniform treatment. Some general background references and the TinyLlama citation are removed, while the principal research positioning remains.

P1.justification: V2 tightens the introduction, creates Section 2.2 for masked-diffusion limitations, separates unconditional generation from self-correction, and moves downstream evaluation to Section 5.5. It adds a contents list and reorganizes appendix headings, including moving the MDM equivalence proof into H.9. Much of the original narrative and overall structure remains.

P2.justification: V2 adds the GPT-4o results table and evaluator-prompt figure, and augments Figures 3, 5, 6 and the former Figure 7 with entropy curves, secondary axes and legends. These substantially expand the generation-related displays. The downstream table is shortened and relocated; unchanged examples and scaling plots are retained.

improvement.justification: V2 better supports the central self-correction claim through diversity checks and GPT-4o grading, supplementing v1's reliance mainly on perplexity and examples. The disclosed prompt and more cautious benchmark interpretation also help. The gains are limited by missing grading sample counts and statistical-calculation details, while the new Equation 65/69 inconsistency prevents treating the expanded mathematics as an unqualified improvement.
